subject: Civil Engineering
title: Tuned Mass Dampers
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Tuned Mass Dampers.

hook.text: Taipei 101 has a 730-ton steel ball hanging near the top — it counteracts swaying.

buildup.text: A tuned mass damper is a heavy weight on springs — tuned to the building's natural frequency.

discovery.text: When the building sways left, the weight swings right — counteracting the motion.

twist.text: TMDs work for both wind and earthquakes — dual-purpose protection in one system.

climax.text: During Typhoon Soudelor in 2015, Taipei 101's damper swung 3 feet — keeping the tower steady.

punchline.text: Fight motion with motion — a swinging weight that calms a swaying tower.

quiz.question: How does a tuned mass damper reduce building sway?
options: It locks the building in place, preventing any movement
A heavy weight swings opposite to the building's motion, counteracting sway
It redirects earthquake waves around the building

details.summary: A tuned mass damper is a large mass mounted on springs or pendulums near the top of a building, tuned to the structure's natural frequency so it swings out of phase with the building during earthquakes or wind.
details.whyItMatters: Tuned mass dampers allow slender, tall buildings to resist both earthquake and wind forces without adding excessive structural material, enabling iconic designs like Taipei 101.
takeaways: A heavy mass tuned to the building's frequency swings opposite to building motion
The countermotion reduces peak building accelerations by 30 to 50 percent
Taipei 101's 730-ton pendulum damper is the most famous example worldwide

faq.question: How does a tuned mass damper reduce building motion?
faq.answer: When the building sways in one direction, the damper mass swings in the opposite direction because it is tuned to the building's natural frequency. This countermotion creates forces that oppose the building's movement, extracting energy from the structural vibration.

faq.question: How large does a tuned mass damper need to be relative to the building?
faq.answer: Effective tuned mass dampers typically have a mass of 0.5 to 5% of the building's total mass. Taipei 101's 730-ton damper is about 0.5% of the building mass. Larger mass ratios provide better vibration reduction but require more space and structural support.
